profile.reading: This facility is attributed in the registry to NTT, part of Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corporation, one of the largest telecommunications and IT services groups in the world, headquartered in Tokyo, Japan. NTT operates a global data center business, NTT Global Data Centers, under NTT DATA, Inc. The operators own about us page, fetched this session, states NTT DATA is a top 10 global IT services provider with about 30 billion dollars in annual revenue, operations across 33 countries, and about 3 billion dollars in annual research and development investment, headquartered at the Toyosu Center Building, 3-3-3 Toyosu, Koto-ku, Tokyo 135-6033, Japan, though these figures describe the wider NTT DATA organization rather than the data center division specifically, and no data center division formation or acquisition date was found on the pages fetched this session. A previously confirmed, specific data center acquisition remains NTT Communications purchase of an 86.7 percent stake in e-shelter, described as Germany top data center operator, completed around June 23, 2015, though that acquisition is not directly connected to this United States facility. This session reached the operators own services.global.ntt data center locations pages directly and successfully. reading.body:
NTT Ashburn VA2 publishes 14 MW of IT capacity. Assuming 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 14 MW supports roughly 350 racks; at 10 kW per rack, a figure more typical of colocation mixed workloads, the same power fills about 1,400 racks. The operator does not publish redundancy tier, PUE, raised-floor area, or connectivity details on the page this site read, so no further physical characterization is possible from the data.

The campus sits in Ashburn, the densest single colocation market in Virginia and among the densest in the world. Against the 19 Virginia facilities for which this site holds a published megawatt figure, VA2 ranks 17th, contributing 14 of the 1,326 published MW, or roughly 1 percent of that subset. Virginia has 326 mapped facilities in total, and most publish no capacity figure, so the 1,326 MW total and the ranking both undercount the actual state inventory.

At 14 MW, VA2 is a mid-to-small facility by the standards of the Ashburn corridor, where hyperscale campuses routinely publish figures one to two orders of magnitude larger. Nothing in the published data indicates the campus is optimized for high-density AI training loads, though nothing rules it out either. A reader evaluating this campus for AI inference or enterprise GPU workloads would need rack-level power density and cooling specifications, neither of which NTT has published on the page this site read.
